tests.title: make build writes agent-fox beside af with the same ldflags
given: a temporary BIN_DIR and make available
tests.when: make build VERSION=9.9.9-test BIN_DIR=<tmp> is run and each binary is run with --version
then: both <tmp>/af and <tmp>/agent-fox exist and are executable
agent-fox --version reports version 9.9.9-test
af --version reports the same version and commit
tests.pseudocode: run('make build VERSION=9.9.9-test BIN_DIR='+tmp); assert exists(tmp/agent-fox) and exists(tmp/af); v=json(run(tmp/agent-fox,'--version')); assert v.version=='9.9.9-test'; assert v.commit==json(run(tmp/af,'--version')).commit

tests.title: --version prints the five-field document and --help prints usage, both exit 0 without reading configuration
given: the agent-fox binary built by make build
no config file anywhere on the lookup path and an empty HOME
tests.when: agent-fox --version and agent-fox --help are run separately
then: --version exits 0 and stdout is exactly one JSON object with name agent-fox, version, commit, build_time and go_version and no other field
--help exits 0 and prints usage mentioning --config, --version and --help
neither run fails for lack of a configuration file
tests.pseudocode: r=run(bin,'--version'); assert r.code==0; d=json(r.stdout); assert keys(d)=={'name','version','commit','build_time','go_version'}; assert d.name=='agent-fox'; h=run(bin,'--help'); assert h.code==0; assert '--config' in (h.stdout+h.stderr)

tests.title: An unknown flag or a positional argument prints plain usage on stderr and exits 2
given: the agent-fox binary
tests.when: agent-fox --bogus and agent-fox extra are run
then: both exit with code 2
stderr is plain-text usage and not a JSON log record
nothing listens and no listening record is written
tests.pseudocode: for args in (['--bogus'],['extra']): r=run(bin,*args); assert r.code==2; assert not parses_as_json(r.stderr); assert 'listening' not in r.stderr

tests.title: Invalid configuration, key or database writes exactly one start failed ERROR record and exits 2
given: a config with unknown key server.external_url
a config whose key file is missing
a config whose database.path is a directory that cannot be opened as a database
tests.when: agent-fox --config <file> is run for each case
then: each run exits 2
stderr holds exactly one line, a JSON slog record with level ERROR and msg 'start failed'
the error attribute names the key or file at fault
no listening record is written and nothing listens
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: r=run(bin,'--config',case.file); assert r.code==2; recs=json_lines(r.stderr); assert len(recs)==1; assert recs[0].level=='ERROR' and recs[0].msg=='start failed'; assert case.needle in recs[0].error

tests.title: A bind failure exits 1 with exactly one start failed ERROR record naming the address
given: a loopback port already held by another listener
a config with server.listen set to that address
a second config with a host that does not resolve
tests.when: agent-fox --config <file> is run for each config
then: each run exits 1
stderr holds exactly one JSON record at level ERROR with msg 'start failed'
the error attribute contains the address and a reason
no listening record is written
tests.pseudocode: ln=net.Listen('127.0.0.1:0'); r=run(bin,'--config',cfg(listen=ln.Addr())); assert r.code==1; recs=json_lines(r.stderr); assert len(recs)==1 and recs[0].msg=='start failed'; assert ln.Addr() in recs[0].error

tests.title: The listening record carries the actually bound address when listen port is 0
given: a valid config with server.listen 127.0.0.1:0
tests.when: agent-fox is started and its stderr is read
then: a JSON record with msg 'listening' appears
its addr attribute is host:port with a non-zero port
GET http://<addr>/healthz answers 200
tests.pseudocode: p=start(bin,cfg); rec=wait_record(p.stderr,'listening'); host,port=split(rec.addr); assert port!='0'; assert get('http://'+rec.addr+'/healthz').status==200

tests.title: SIGTERM and SIGINT drain in-flight requests, close the database and exit 0
given: a running agent-fox whose fake hub delays GET /api/v1/user by about one second
a request in flight that needs that hub call
tests.when: SIGTERM is sent while the request is in flight (and, in a second run, SIGINT)
then: the in-flight request completes with its normal response
new connections are refused after the signal
the process exits 0 well before 30 seconds
tests.pseudocode: p=start(bin,cfg); fut=async(get(addr+'/api/v1/workspaces',bearer='t')); sleep(200ms); p.signal(SIGTERM); assert fut.result().status==200; assert p.wait()==0; assert connect(addr).refused

tests.title: A listener failure after start is logged at ERROR and the run function returns exit code 1
given: the service run function with a listener whose Accept fails after start
a real opened store
tests.when: the run function serves and the listener returns a non-shutdown error
then: an ERROR record is logged
the database is closed
the returned exit code is 1
tests.pseudocode: code=run(cfg, listener=failingListener()); assert code==1; assert 'ERROR' in logs; assert store.closed

tests.title: Config lookup prefers --config, then ./config.toml, then XDG then HOME/.config
given: temp directories holding distinct config files at each lookup location
XDG_CONFIG_HOME set in one case and unset in another with HOME pointing to a temp dir
tests.when: the loader is called with an explicit path, then with none from a working directory with and without ./config.toml
then: an explicit path wins over every other file
./config.toml wins over the XDG file
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agent-fox/config.toml is used when set
$HOME/.config/agent-fox/config.toml is used when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset
tests.pseudocode: assert Load(explicit).Hub.URL=='http://explicit'; chdir(withLocal); assert Load('').Hub.URL=='http://local'; chdir(empty); setenv(XDG,x); assert Load('').Hub.URL=='http://xdg'; unsetenv(XDG); assert Load('').Hub.URL=='http://home'

tests.title: A missing config lists every path tried and invalid TOML names the file and position
given: no --config and no file at any lookup path
a --config pointing to a nonexistent file
a --config file with a TOML syntax error on line 3
tests.when: the loader is called in each case
then: the first error contains every lookup path tried
the second error names the file
the third error names the file and the line/column of the parse error
the binary run for each case exits 2
tests.pseudocode: err=Load(''); for p in lookupPaths: assert p in err.Error(); err=Load(badToml); assert file in err.Error() and 'line 3' in err.Error()

tests.title: A minimal config gets defaults, a trailing slash dropped and relative paths resolved against the config directory
given: a config in a temp dir setting only hub.url = http://hub.local:9000/ and secrets.key_file = key
XDG_STATE_HOME set to a temp dir, then unset with HOME set
tests.when: the config is loaded
then: server.listen is 127.0.0.1:8090
hub.auth_cache_ttl is 60s
hub.url has no trailing slash
secrets.key_file is the absolute path <config dir>/key
database.path is $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox/agent-fox.db, or $HOME/.local/state/agent-fox/agent-fox.db when unset
a relative database.path is resolved against the config file's directory
tests.pseudocode: c=Load(f); assert c.Server.Listen=='127.0.0.1:8090'; assert c.Hub.AuthCacheTTL==60s; assert c.Hub.URL=='http://hub.local:9000'; assert c.Secrets.KeyFile==join(dir,'key'); assert c.Database.Path==join(xdg,'agent-fox/agent-fox.db')

tests.title: ${NAME} is expanded in decoded string values and an empty variable expands to empty
given: environment HUBHOST=hub.local and KEYDIR=/k and EMPTYVAR set to empty
a config with hub.url = "http://${HUBHOST}:1" and secrets.key_file = "${KEYDIR}/key"
a second config with secrets.key_file = "${EMPTYVAR}"
tests.when: each config is loaded
then: the first config holds http://hub.local:1 and /k/key
the second fails as secrets.key_file missing/empty rather than as an unset variable
a $ not followed by {NAME} is left alone
tests.pseudocode: c=Load(f1); assert c.Hub.URL=='http://hub.local:1'; assert c.Secrets.KeyFile=='/k/key'; err=Load(f2); assert 'secrets.key_file' in err.Error()

tests.title: An unset ${VAR} fails start naming the variable and the key, exit 2
given: a config with hub.url = "${NO_SUCH_VAR_XYZ}" and the variable unset
tests.when: agent-fox --config <file> is run
then: exit code 2
exactly one ERROR 'start failed' record
its error attribute contains NO_SUCH_VAR_XYZ and hub.url
tests.pseudocode: r=run(bin,'--config',f); assert r.code==2; e=json_lines(r.stderr)[0].error; assert 'NO_SUCH_VAR_XYZ' in e and 'hub.url' in e

tests.title: Unknown keys and wrong-typed values are refused naming the dotted key, exit 2
given: configs adding server.external_url, a [workers] table with count, database.retain, a misspelt hub.auth_cach_ttl, and hub.url = 5 (wrong type)
tests.when: agent-fox --config <file> is run for each config
then: each run exits 2
the error attribute contains the dotted key: server.external_url, workers.count (or workers), database.retain, hub.auth_cach_ttl, hub.url
tests.pseudocode: for c in cases: r=run(bin,'--config',c.file); assert r.code==2; assert c.key in json_lines(r.stderr)[0].error

tests.title: auth_cache_ttl is accepted from 1s to 15m inclusive and refused outside without clamping
given: configs with hub.auth_cache_ttl of 500ms, 1s, 15m, 16m and a non-duration string
tests.when: each is loaded
then: 1s and 15m load with exactly those values
500ms, 16m and the non-duration string fail with an error containing hub.auth_cache_ttl
no refused value is clamped into range
tests.pseudocode: assert Load(ttl('1s')).Hub.AuthCacheTTL==1s; assert Load(ttl('15m')).Hub.AuthCacheTTL==15m; for v in ('500ms','16m','x'): assert 'hub.auth_cache_ttl' in Load(ttl(v)).Error()

tests.title: Missing or malformed hub.url, key_file and server.listen are refused naming the dotted key
given: configs with hub.url missing, empty, relative, ftp://x, with ?q=1, with #frag
a config with secrets.key_file missing
a config with server.listen = "nocolon"
tests.when: each is loaded
then: each fails with an error containing the dotted key hub.url, secrets.key_file or server.listen
a hub.url with a path prefix such as https://h/prefix is accepted
server.listen 127.0.0.1:0 is accepted
tests.pseudocode: for c in bad: assert c.key in Load(c.file).Error(); assert Load(prefixed).Hub.URL=='https://h/prefix'

tests.title: A non-loopback http hub.url logs a WARN after bind and before listening
given: a config with hub.url = http://hub.example.internal:8080
a second config with hub.url = http://127.0.0.1:1
a valid key file and a temp database
tests.when: agent-fox is started with each config and its stderr read until the listening record
then: the first run starts and logs a WARN record saying tokens cross the link in clear, before the listening record
the second run logs no such WARN
a failed start in the first config writes only its one ERROR record and no WARN
tests.pseudocode: recs=records_until(p.stderr,'listening'); assert index(recs,level=='WARN') < index(recs,msg=='listening'); assert no_warn(second)

tests.title: A missing, non-base64 or wrong-length key file fails naming the file and never its contents
given: a key path that does not exist
a 0600 key file with the text 'not base64 !!!secretmarker'
a 0600 key file holding base64 of 31 bytes and one holding 33 bytes
tests.when: the key loader is called for each, and agent-fox is run for the missing case
then: each returns an error containing the key file path
no error contains the file's contents
a valid file with surrounding whitespace/newline loads
the binary exits 2 with the path in the error attribute for the missing file
tests.pseudocode: for f in bad: err=LoadKey(f); assert f in err.Error(); assert 'secretmarker' not in err.Error(); assert LoadKey(valid_with_newline) ok

tests.title: Key files with group or other permission bits are refused and owner-only modes accepted
given: valid key files chmodded to 0644, 0640, 0600, 0400 and 0700 (non-Windows)
tests.when: the key loader is called for each
then: 0644 and 0640 fail with an error naming the file and its mode
0600, 0400 and 0700 load successfully
starting the binary with the 0644 file exits 2
tests.pseudocode: for m in (0o644,0o640): chmod(f,m); err=LoadKey(f); assert f in err and oct(m) in err; for m in (0o600,0o400,0o700): chmod(f,m); assert LoadKey(f) ok

tests.title: A sealed value has version byte 0x01, a 12-byte nonce and ciphertext plus tag
given: a 32-byte key and a sealer
tests.when: a token of known length is sealed for a slug
then: the first byte is 0x01
total length is 1 + 12 + len(token) + 16
the bytes do not contain the plaintext
the value opens only when additional data agent-fox/subscription/<slug> is used (decrypting by hand with AES-GCM succeeds)
tests.pseudocode: s=Seal('widgets',tok); assert s[0]==1 and len(s)==1+12+len(tok)+16; assert tok not in s; assert gcm.Open(nil,s[1:13],s[13:],'agent-fox/subscription/widgets')==tok

tests.title: Sealing then opening round-trips and two seals of the same token differ
given: a random 32-byte key and a seed taken from the test
tests.when: for any token (including empty-adjacent, unicode and long strings) and any valid slug, it is sealed twice and opened
then: open(slug, seal(slug, token)) returns the token with the same key
the two seals of the same token differ
tests.pseudocode: for tok,slug in gen(): a=Seal(slug,tok); b=Seal(slug,tok); assert Open(slug,a)==tok; assert a!=b

tests.title: Opening fails with an error, never a panic, for a wrong key, altered byte, other slug, unknown version or truncation
given: a sealed value for slug widgets under key A
tests.when: it is opened with key B, with each single byte flipped, under slug gadgets, with version byte 0x02, and truncated to every length from 0 to len-1
then: every attempt returns a non-nil error and empty plaintext
no attempt panics
tests.pseudocode: for variant in variants: pt,err=Open(variant); assert err!=nil and pt==''; for n in range(len(s)): assert Open(s[:n]) errors

tests.title: Neither the key nor a plaintext token appears in logs, errors or files outside the sealed column
given: a running service against a fake hub with a distinctive key and a distinctive PAT
failing cases: wrong PAT, hub 500, unreadable token
tests.when: a subscription is created and read, failures are provoked, and stderr, error bodies, the database file and WAL and the data directory files are scanned
then: the key's base64 and raw bytes appear nowhere
the plaintext PAT appears in no stderr line, no error body, and no file except via the AEAD ciphertext (not as bytes)
tests.pseudocode: run_scenario(); for blob in (stderr, error_bodies, read(db), read(db+'-wal')): assert key_b64 not in blob and key_raw not in blob and PAT not in blob

tests.title: Opening a new database creates a 0700 directory, a 0600 file and sets the pragmas
given: a database path inside a directory that does not exist
tests.when: the store is opened and the pragmas queried
then: the parent directory has mode 0700 and the file mode 0600
PRAGMA journal_mode returns wal
PRAGMA busy_timeout returns 5000
PRAGMA foreign_keys returns 1 (on a fresh connection from the pool as well)
tests.pseudocode: s=Open(path); assert mode(dir)==0o700 and mode(path)==0o600; assert q('PRAGMA journal_mode')=='wal'; assert q('PRAGMA busy_timeout')==5000; assert q('PRAGMA foreign_keys')==1

tests.title: Every owned table is af_-prefixed, user_version is untouched and a foreign table is never changed
given: a database pre-populated with a table named jobs with rows and PRAGMA user_version set to 42
tests.when: the store is opened, subscriptions are written and read, and the schema inspected
then: every table in sqlite_master other than the foreign jobs table starts with af_
PRAGMA user_version is still 42
the jobs table and its rows are unchanged
the migration record lives in an af_-prefixed table
tests.pseudocode: seed(jobs, user_version=42); s=Open(path); put_get_delete(s); for t in tables: assert t=='jobs' or t.startswith('af_'); assert user_version()==42; assert rows(jobs)==seed

tests.title: Migrations apply once in order and reopening applies nothing
given: an empty database path
tests.when: the store is opened twice
then: after the first open the migration record lists migration 1
after the second open each migration is listed exactly once
a migration that fails midway leaves no partial change (its transaction rolls back)
tests.pseudocode: Open(p).Close(); Open(p).Close(); rows=q('select version from af_schema_migrations'); assert rows==[1]; assert failing_migration_rolled_back()

tests.title: A database recording a newer migration than the binary knows fails start naming both versions and is unchanged
given: a database whose migration record holds version 999 while the binary knows 1
tests.when: the store is opened and agent-fox --config is run on it
then: the store error names 999 and the known version
the binary exits 2 with a start failed record containing both numbers
the file bytes are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: seed_version(999); before=sha(db); r=run(bin,cfg); assert r.code==2; e=json_lines(r.stderr)[0].error; assert '999' in e and '1' in e; assert sha(db)==before

tests.title: A database that cannot be created or opened fails start with database.path in the error, exit 2
given: database.path under a parent that is a regular file
database.path that is a file of non-SQLite garbage
tests.when: agent-fox --config is run for each
then: each exits 2
the error attribute of the single ERROR record contains the database path
tests.pseudocode: for p in bad_paths: r=run(bin,cfg(db=p)); assert r.code==2; assert p in json_lines(r.stderr)[0].error

tests.title: Migration 1 creates a subscriptions table with unique slug and RFC 3339 UTC times
given: a freshly migrated store
tests.when: two rows with the same slug are inserted directly and a row is stored through the store API
then: the table has columns for slug, label prefix, sealed token, token user (nullable), subscribed by and created/updated times
the second insert of the same slug violates uniqueness
stored created_at and updated_at parse as RFC 3339 and end in Z (UTC)
tests.pseudocode: assert dup_insert fails with unique error; row=get('widgets'); t=time.Parse(RFC3339,row.created_at); assert t.Location()==UTC

tests.title: The hub client sends the two GET calls with bearer, accept and user-agent headers and an escaped slug
given: an httptest server recording requests and a client with version 1.2.3
tests.when: User(ctx, 'tok') and Workspace(ctx, 'tok', 'a b/c?') are called
then: the paths are /api/v1/user and /api/v1/workspaces/a%20b%2Fc%3F under the configured base path prefix
method is GET
Authorization is 'Bearer tok', Accept is application/json, User-Agent is agent-fox/1.2.3
no other path is requested
tests.pseudocode: c.User(ctx,'tok'); c.Workspace(ctx,'tok','a b/c?'); r=srv.requests; assert r[0].path=='/api/v1/user'; assert r[1].rawpath=='/api/v1/workspaces/a%20b%2Fc%3F'; assert r[0].header['Authorization']=='Bearer tok'

tests.title: The hub client times out after 10 seconds or the context deadline, caps bodies at 1 MiB and does not follow redirects
given: a server that hangs, a server answering 302 to a second server, and a server sending a body larger than 1 MiB
tests.when: calls are made with a long context and with a 50ms context, and the redirect and large body are requested
then: the client's default timeout is 10s and a 50ms context ends the call in about 50ms as unavailable
the second server in the redirect receives no request, so the token never reaches another host
at most 1 MiB of the large body is read and the answer is unavailable
tests.pseudocode: assert c.HTTP.Timeout==10s; err=c.User(ctx50ms,'t'); assert Unavailable(err); c.User(ctx,'t') on 302; assert target.requests==0; assert bytes_read<=1<<20+1

tests.title: A 200 user object yields the id as a string whether sent as a string or number, and a 200 workspace is found
given: a hub answering {"id":"usr_1","login":"ann"}, {"id":42}, and a workspace object {"slug":"widgets"}
tests.when: User and Workspace are called
then: the first user has id usr_1 and login ann
the numeric id is kept as the string "42" with empty login
Workspace returns without error (found)
tests.pseudocode: assert c.User()=={id:'usr_1',login:'ann'}; assert c.User()=={id:'42',login:''}; assert c.Workspace() err==nil

tests.title: Hub 401, 403 and 404 map to refused, not found and unavailable per call
given: a hub answering each of 401, 403, 404 for both calls
tests.when: User and Workspace are called for each status
then: user: 401 refused, 403 refused, 404 unavailable
workspace: 401 refused, 403 not found, 404 not found
each error is classified by errors.Is/As with no message parsing
tests.pseudocode: table={('user',401):Refused,('user',403):Refused,('user',404):Unavailable,('ws',401):Refused,('ws',403):NotFound,('ws',404):NotFound}; for (call,st),want in table: assert classify(call(st))==want

tests.title: 3xx, 429, 5xx, transport errors, timeouts and bad 200 bodies are all unavailable
given: a hub answering 301, 302, 429, 500, 503, hanging up, answering 200 with non-JSON, 200 with a JSON array, 200 user without id, 200 user with empty id
tests.when: User is called for each and Workspace for the status and body cases
then: every case is classified unavailable and none as refused or not found
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: assert classify(c.User(case))==Unavailable; for case in status_and_body_cases: assert classify(c.Workspace(case))==Unavailable

tests.title: Hub errors are told apart by errors.Is or errors.As and never contain the token
given: failures of each class produced by a fake hub, with token 'tok-SECRET-123'
tests.when: errors from User and Workspace are inspected
then: errors.Is(err, ErrRefused) or errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) or errors.As(err, *UnavailableError) identifies the class
the three classes are mutually exclusive
err.Error() does not contain the token, including for transport errors that embed the URL
tests.pseudocode: for err in errs: assert exactly_one(is_refused(err),is_notfound(err),is_unavailable(err)); assert 'tok-SECRET-123' not in err.Error()

tests.title: No hub error message ever contains the token
given: a fake hub that can answer any status or hang up, seeded from the test
tests.when: for any token of printable characters (length 8 to 64) and any failure mode (status, hangup, bad body, timeout), a hub call is made
then: err.Error() never contains the token
tests.pseudocode: for tok,mode in gen(): err=call(tok,mode); assert err==nil or tok not in err.Error()

tests.title: A missing, non-Bearer or empty-token Authorization header is answered 401 without calling hub
given: a service with a fake hub that counts requests
tests.when: GET /api/v1/workspaces is sent with no header, 'Basic abc', 'Bearer' and 'Bearer ' (empty token), and with 'bearer tok' lowercase
then: the first four answer 401 with error code unauthenticated
the hub request count is zero after those four
lowercase 'bearer tok' is accepted as the scheme and reaches hub
tests.pseudocode: for h in bad: r=get('/api/v1/workspaces',auth=h); assert r.status==401 and r.json.error.code=='unauthenticated'; assert hub.total()==0; get(auth='bearer tok'); assert hub.count('/api/v1/user',hash('tok'))==1

tests.title: A validated caller token is not sent to /user again within the TTL and is sent again after it
given: a service with auth_cache_ttl 60s and an injectable clock
a fake hub mapping token t1 to a user
tests.when: three requests are made with t1 within the TTL, the clock advances past the TTL, and a fourth request is made
then: the hub's /api/v1/user count for hash(t1) is 1 after the first three requests
it is 2 after the fourth
the cache key is the hex SHA-256 of the token (the raw token is not a key)
tests.pseudocode: for i in 3: get(t1); assert hub.count('/api/v1/user',h(t1))==1; clock.advance(61s); get(t1); assert hub.count('/api/v1/user',h(t1))==2

tests.title: A token hub refused answers 401 and is not sent again within the TTL
given: a service with a TTL and a fake hub that refuses token bad with 401
tests.when: two requests are made with the bad token, the clock advances past the TTL and a third is made
then: both first requests answer 401 unauthenticated
hub saw /api/v1/user once for the token after two requests
hub saw it twice after the TTL
tests.pseudocode: assert get(bad).status==401; assert get(bad).status==401; assert hub.count(user,h(bad))==1; clock.advance(ttl+1); get(bad); assert hub.count(user,h(bad))==2

tests.title: Hub unavailable on identity or visibility answers 502 and caches nothing
given: a fake hub failing /api/v1/user with 500 for token t, and later failing /api/v1/workspaces/widgets with 503 for a validated caller
tests.when: a request is made, hub recovers, and the request is repeated
then: the first answers 502 hub_unavailable
the repeat calls hub again and succeeds
the visibility outage also answers 502 and the next request calls hub's workspace endpoint again
tests.pseudocode: hub.fail('/api/v1/user',500); assert get(t).status==502 and code=='hub_unavailable'; hub.clear(); assert get(t).status==200; assert hub.count(user,h(t))==2

tests.title: A hidden workspace answers 404 byte-identical to an unsubscribed one, with visibility cached per (token, slug)
given: widgets subscribed; caller A sees widgets on hub; caller B does not; slug ghost is subscribed nowhere and visible to nobody
a service with a TTL and injectable clock
tests.when: B requests GET /api/v1/workspaces/widgets and A requests GET /api/v1/workspaces/ghost-visible-but-unsubscribed, B repeats the request, then the clock advances
then: both answer 404 not_found with byte-identical bodies (apart from nothing slug-specific)
B's repeat is served from the visibility cache (hub workspace count for B,widgets stays 1)
after the TTL hub's workspace count becomes 2
a found workspace for A is also cached for the TTL
tests.pseudocode: r1=get('/api/v1/workspaces/widgets',B); r2=get('/api/v1/workspaces/zzz',A); assert r1.body==r2.body and r1.status==404; get(B); assert hub.count(ws('widgets'),h(B))==1

tests.title: The slug syntax is checked first, before identity, with 400 invalid_request
given: a service and a fake hub counting requests
tests.when: GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug> is sent with an invalid slug ('-bad', 'a b', a 101-character slug, 'x!') and an invalid token
then: every invalid slug answers 400 invalid_request even with an unauthenticated token
hub receives no request for them
slugs 'a', 'A.b_c-1' and a 100-character slug pass the syntax check
tests.pseudocode: for s in bad: r=get('/api/v1/workspaces/'+s,'Bearer nope'); assert r.status==400 and r.json.error.code=='invalid_request'; assert hub.total()==0

tests.title: A hub 401 on a caller-token call evicts the identity and all visibility entries
given: caller token t validated and cached, and visibility cached for widgets and gadgets
then hub answers 401 to the workspace call for gizmos made with t
tests.when: GET /api/v1/workspaces/gizmos is sent, then GET /api/v1/workspaces/widgets with the same token
then: the first answers 401 unauthenticated
the next request calls GET /api/v1/user again
the visibility for widgets and gadgets is fetched again (counts increase)
